summary: Reviewed the full test_nodes.py file including the new TestSlimPromptContent class (lines 997–1221). The 16 new tests are well-structured, correctly isolated, and follow the established patterns in the file. _IDENTITY_PHRASES sentinel list is module-level (reusable); _build_slim_state() helper avoids duplication across 16 tests; PM and synthesis tests correctly handle the no-wp_id distinction. All five acceptance criteria confirmed. pytest independently verified: 120/120 pass, 0 failures.

comments.note: The _IDENTITY_PHRASES module-level sentinel list (line 1003) is a sound extensibility choice. When a new node is added, the list can be updated once and all 8 identity-absence tests benefit automatically. No duplication across test cases.

The _build_slim_state() helper (line 1017) correctly reuses base_state() and avoids 16 instances of manual dict construction. The _SLIM_PROJECT_PATH and _SLIM_WP_ID constants make assertions unambiguous — no magic strings scattered through the tests.

The PM and synthesis tests correctly diverge from the 6 pipeline-stage nodes: PM uses a tmp_path fixture to provide a real plan file (no temp file = OSError fallback path, not tested here but covered in TestPMNodePromptIncludesPlanContent); synthesis passes current_wp_id='' and calls _assert_slim_fields_present with expect_wp=False. Both are correct and consistent with the WP-002 and WP-003 specs.

The _assert_slim_fields_present helper checks three distinct signals: (1) the actual project_path value, (2) the literal string 'CRITICAL', and (3) the literal string 'project_path' — this triple-check is robust against a prompt that mentions CRITICAL for unrelated reasons, since all three must co-occur to pass. Well designed.

The module docstring on line 1 of test_nodes.py still references 'six Deep Agent stage nodes' — after WP-001/002/003 there are 8 (pm, developer, qa, reviewer, security_auditor, release_engineer, docs, synthesis). Worth updating to 'eight' or 'all orchestrator stage nodes'.
